mainTopic: Age limits for כהנים and other roles, the definitions of 'old' and 'young', and how a כלי חרס becomes טמא through its airspace.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the proof that the לויים had to sing together in one voice. It then defines 'old' for a כהן as the point when he begins to tremble. A משנה about a בעל קרי who immersed before urinating leads the גמרא to define 'young': anyone who can stand on one foot and take off or put on his shoe. A story follows about רבי חנינא, who could still do this at eighty and credited his mother's care. Next, ברייתות discuss when a man may lead the community and when a כהן may begin the עבודה. One view says from שתי שערות, and רבי says from twenty, based on a פסוק in עזרא. The גמרא then gives two versions of how the custom of waiting until twenty fits these views. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a כלי חרס becomes טמא through its airspace, while other כלים become טמא through their outside. The גמרא begins tracing this to the word 'תוכו', and רבי יונתן's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse showing the Levites sang as one voice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק that serves as the source for disqualifying a לוי whose voice cannot blend with the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: "It came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the previous lines. It quotes a פסוק showing that the לויים had to sing together as one voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion said a לוי can be disqualified because of his voice. This פסוק is the source: the singers had to produce 'one sound,' so a לוי whose voice cannot join the group is unfit for the singing.

keyTerms.meaning: Singers (the לויים who sang in the מקדש)

phrases.english: "It came to pass, when the trumpeters
and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the scriptural source for the voice disqualification discussed just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: A לוי whose voice cannot blend with the others is unfit to sing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 5:13, 'to make one sound to be heard'

steps.title: How old is 'until he ages'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define the point at which a כהן is too old to serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Until he ages': until when?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא said a כהן is fit to serve 'until he ages.' The גמרא asks what that means in practice, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Old' is a vague word. The גמרא wants a clear, testable sign of when old age begins to disqualify a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Until when? How far does this go?

phrases.english: 'Until he ages': until when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the לויים's voice to the age limit for כהנים in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of 'old age' that ends a כהן's fitness.

steps.title: Old means when he starts to tremble
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא defines old age as the point when the כהן begins to tremble.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעא said in the name of רבי חנינא: until he trembles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A כהן counts as 'old' once he begins to shake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is not a set number of years. It is a physical sign: once his hands and feet shake, he can no longer serve properly.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ela said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Until he trembles.
phrases.notes: He means the shaking of hands and feet that comes with old age.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא עַד שֶׁיְּרַתֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Old age that ends a כהן's fitness begins when he trembles.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן serves until he begins to tremble. Physical ability, not a set age, is the test.

steps.title: A בעל קרי who immersed before urinating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a בעל קרי who immersed without first urinating becomes impure when he urinates. רבי יוסי makes this depend on whether the man is old or sick versus young or healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: A בעל קרי who immersed but did not urinate first becomes impure when he urinates. רבי יוסי says: if he is sick or old, he is impure; if he is young or healthy, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different משנה that also uses the idea of 'old' versus 'young.' It is setting up another 'how young?' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says leftover זרע may come out with the urine, so he becomes impure again. רבי יוסי says that worry applies only to a sick or old person. A young, healthy person releases it all at once, so he stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission
A sick person and a healthy person

steps.confusionAlert: The impurity does not come from the urine itself. The worry is that leftover זרע comes out together with the urine.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מקואות 8:4.

phrases.english: One who had a seminal emission who immersed
and did not urinate,
when he urinates, he is impure.
phrases.notes: Leftover זרע comes out with the urine, so he becomes impure again.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
In a sick person and an old person, he is impure;
in a young person and a healthy person, he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם בַּעַל קֶרִי שֶׁטָּבַל וְלֹא הֵטִיל מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another case where the line between old and young matters, defined by the same רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion: he becomes impure when he urinates. רבי יוסי: only a sick or old person; a young or healthy person stays pure.

steps.title: Until when is someone 'young'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define the 'young' person in רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young person: until when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear test of who counts as 'young' in רבי יוסי's ruling. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the כהן, 'young' needs a practical measure. The answer decides who stays pure after urinating.

keyTerms.meaning: A young person (here, someone still vigorous, not a child)

phrases.english: A young person: until when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term in the משנה of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The test for being 'young' in רבי יוסי's ruling.

steps.title: Young means able to stand on one foot and handle a shoe
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says anyone who can stand on one foot and take off or put on his shoe counts as young.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעא said in the name of רבי חנינא: anyone who can stand on one foot and take off his shoe or put on his shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical physical test for being 'young.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the measure is strength and balance, not age in years. Someone who still has this control counts as 'young' for רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: Both definitions come from רבי חנינא, and both use a physical test. Old means trembling; young means being able to stand on one foot and take off or put on a shoe.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ela said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Anyone who stands on one of his legs
and removes his shoe or puts on his shoe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא כֹּל שֶׁעוֹמֵד עַל רַגְלוֹ אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Young means able to stand on one foot and take off or put on a shoe.

steps.title: רבי חנינא could still do it at eighty
steps.stepSummary: A report that רבי חנינא himself, at eighty, could stand on one foot and take off or put on his shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי חנינא that he was eighty years old, and he would stand on one foot and take off his shoe and put on his shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רבי חנינא, who gave the test. At eighty he could still pass it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the test really is about physical ability, not age. Even an eighty-year-old can count as 'young' by this measure.

phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Ḥanina
that he was eighty years old
and he would stand on one of his legs
and remove his shoe and put on his shoe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the test of step 6 with רבי חנינא himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא could pass his own 'youth' test at age eighty.

steps.title: רבי חנינא credits his mother's care
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the hot water and oil his mother rubbed on him as a child gave him strength in old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: the hot water and oil my mother smeared on me in my youth stood by me in my old age.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא explains why he was still so strong at eighty: his mother's care when he was a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the story. His strength in old age came from being bathed in hot water and rubbed with oil as a child.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The hot water and oil that my mother smeared on me in my youth
they stood by me in my old age.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא חַמִּין וָשֶׁמֶן שֶׁסָּכַתְנִי אִמִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חנינא explains the strength described in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Care in childhood, hot water and oil, preserved רבי חנינא's strength into old age.

steps.title: A full beard qualifies a man to lead the community
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that once a man's beard has filled out, he may serve as שליח ציבור, lead the prayers, and say ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Once a man's beard is full, he is fit to be appointed a community representative, to go down before the ark to lead the prayers, and to lift his hands for ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets a 'maturity' marker, a full beard, for public leadership roles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier lines dealt with physical signs of age and strength. This ברייתא adds another physical sign, a full beard, as the point when a man is mature enough to represent the community.

keyTerms.meaning: his beard has filled out, a sign of full adulthood
the representative of the community, especially the one who leads prayers
to go down before the ark, meaning to lead the תפילה
lifting the hands, meaning ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If his beard has filled out,
he is fit to be made a representative of the community,
and to go down before the ark,
phrases.notes: This means leading the prayers. The חזן's spot was lower than the rest of the shul.

phrases.english: and to lift his hands.
phrases.notes: This is ברכת כהנים, where the כהנים raise their hands to bless the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining 'young' and 'old' to another age-based rule, this time about leading the community.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man with a full beard may serve as שליח ציבור and do נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: When a כהן becomes fit for Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא asks when a כהן may do עבודה. The תנא קמא says once he has שתי שערות, and רבי says only at twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when is a כהן fit for the Temple service? From when he grows two hairs. רבי says: I say, not until he is twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new question about the minimum age for עבודה, and two opinions disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא ties fitness for עבודה to physical adulthood (שתי שערות, around thirteen). רבי sets a much later age, twenty. This disagreement sets up the next steps, where the גמרא looks for רבי's source.

keyTerms.meaning: the service in the בית המקדש
two pubic hairs, the halachic sign of physical adulthood

phrases.english: From when is he fit for the service?
From when he grows two hairs.
רבי says: I say,
not until he is twenty years old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא continues with a second age question, this time about עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a כהן is fit for עבודה from שתי שערות. רבי: only from age twenty.

steps.title: Asking for רבי's source
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what the reason is for רבי's view that a כהן must be twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is רבי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא sets up the next move by asking where רבי gets the age of twenty. He answers himself right away in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty is not an obvious number for adulthood, since halacha usually uses שתי שערות. So the age needs a source from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason, meaning what is the source

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
What is the reason of רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of רבי's opinion from Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring a כהן to be twenty before doing עבודה.

steps.title: The פסוק in עזרא about age twenty
steps.stepSummary: רבי's source is a פסוק in עזרא saying the לויים were appointed from age twenty to oversee the work of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they appointed the לויים, from twenty years old and up, to oversee the work of the House of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers his own question with a פסוק that mentions the age of twenty for Temple work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links Temple work to the age of twenty. רבי learns from this that no one may do עבודה before twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: the work of the House of ה׳

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And they appointed the לויים,'
phrases.notes: עזרא 3:8. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: from twenty years old and up,
to oversee the work of the House of ה׳.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי's source is עזרא 3:8, which sets twenty as the age for Temple work.

steps.title: The other opinion: overseeing is different
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא explains the פסוק differently. It is about overseeing, which needs an older person, not about the עבודה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other תנא? He holds that 'overseeing' is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the תנא קמא gets around רבי's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does say twenty, but only for 'לנצח,' supervising others. Being in charge needs more maturity than simply doing the עבודה. So the פסוק does not set the age for ordinary service.

keyTerms.meaning: the other one, here the תנא קמא

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: He means the תנא קמא, who says שתי שערות is enough.

phrases.english: 'To oversee' is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the opposing view reads the פסוק from Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק sets twenty only for supervising roles, not for regular עבודה.

steps.title: The פסוק is about לויים, not כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's source: the פסוק speaks about לויים, so how can it teach a rule for כהנים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is written about לויים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from Step 12. The פסוק names לויים, while the argument is about כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לויים and כהנים are different groups with different jobs and different age rules. A פסוק about לויים does not seem to say anything about a כהן's עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: members of the tribe of לוי who are not כהנים
but surely, an opening word for a challenge

phrases.english: But isn't this פסוק written about לויים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's use of עזרא 3:8 as a source for רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names לויים, so it cannot set the age for a כהן's עבודה.

steps.title: כהנים are sometimes called לויים
steps.stepSummary: Based on רבי יהושע בן לוי, there are twenty-four places in תנ״ך where כהנים are called 'לויים,' so the פסוק in עזרא can be about כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: In twenty-four places כהנים are called 'לויים,' and this is one of them: 'And the כהנים the לויים, the sons of צדוק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the word 'לויים' in a פסוק can refer to כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים are part of the tribe of לוי, and תנ״ך sometimes calls them לויים. The פסוק from יחזקאל shows this clearly. So the פסוק in עזרא can also be read as talking about כהנים, and רבי's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the sons of צדוק, a family of כהנים

phrases.english: It follows רבי יהושע בן לוי,
for רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
In twenty-four places
the כהנים are called 'לויים,'
and this is one of them:
'And the כהנים the לויים, the sons of צדוק.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:15. Here the same people are clearly called both כהנים and לויים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'לויים' in עזרא means only regular לויים, so it says nothing about כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לויים' can mean כהנים, as it does in twenty-four places, so the פסוק can be the source for a כהן's age.

steps.title: A קטן is פסול for עבודה
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from 'איש מזרעך' that a minor כהן cannot do עבודה, even if he has no blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Any man of your descendants throughout their generations.' From here רבי אלעזר said: A minor is unfit for the service, even if he is unblemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives a פסוק for the lower limit: a קטן may not do עבודה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'איש,' a man. That word leaves out a child. So even a קטן with no מום is פסול, because the problem is his age and not a blemish.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Any man of your descendants throughout their generations,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:17. The key word is 'איש,' a man, which leaves out a child.

phrases.english: from here רבי אלעזר said:
A minor is unfit for the service, even if he is unblemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that gives a פסוק for the lower age limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן כהן is פסול for עבודה even without a מום.

steps.title: Fit at puberty, but in practice they wait until twenty
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that a כהן is fit from שתי שערות, but his fellow כהנים do not let him serve until he is twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when is he fit for the service? From when he grows two hairs. But his brothers the כהנים do not allow him to serve until he is twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets the line between what is allowed by law and what is done in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By law, a כהן becomes כשר at שתי שערות, like the תנא קמא in Step 10. Age twenty, like רבי's number, appears here only as a custom of the כהנים, not as a rule that makes a younger כהן's עבודה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: his brothers the כהנים, meaning his fellow כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: a קטן is פסול. From שתי שערות a כהן is legally כשר for עבודה. In practice the other כהנים wait until he is twenty. The next two steps ask whose view this ברייתא is.
steps.confusionAlert: Twenty in this ברייתא is a practice of the כהנים, not a law. If a כהן with שתי שערות did serve before twenty, the ברייתא does not say his עבודה is פסול.

phrases.english: From when is he fit for the service?
From when he grows two hairs,
but his brothers the כהנים
do not allow him to serve
until he is twenty years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים אֵין מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of Step 16 by setting when the כהן becomes fit and adding the practice of waiting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is legally כשר from שתי שערות, but his fellow כהנים wait until he is twenty before letting him serve.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא keeps the legal age at puberty while still giving age twenty a role, as a custom of the כהנים.

steps.title: First version: the ברייתא follows רבי, with no disqualification at all
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says the ברייתא is רבי's view, and he holds there is not even a rabbinic disqualification for a young כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this ברייתא follows רבי, and he holds that a כהן under twenty is not disqualified, not even by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא from the last step is. The first answer is that it is רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי's 'until twenty' is only a practice: the fellow כהנים hold him back, exactly as the ברייתא says. It is not a real פסול, not even a rabbinic one, so if he served before twenty his עבודה would be fully valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A disqualification made by the חכמים, not from the תורה

phrases.english: There are those who say:
This is the view of רבי,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the ברייתא from the last step: the fellow כהנים don't let him serve until twenty.

phrases.english: and he does not hold of even a rabbinic disqualification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose opinion the ברייתא of Step 17 follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, a כהן from שתי שערות to twenty has no disqualification at all, not even a rabbinic one.

steps.title: Second version: the ברייתא follows the רבנן, and after-the-fact service is valid
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says רבי does hold a rabbinic disqualification, so the ברייתא must be the רבנן: a young כהן should not serve at first, but if he did, his עבודה counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say רבי does hold that a young כהן is disqualified by rabbinic law, so this ברייתא follows the רבנן. They say he should not serve from the start, but if he already served, his עבודה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who the ברייתא follows. This time it is the רבנן, not רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבי holds a real rabbinic פסול for a כהן under twenty. That does not fit the ברייתא's soft wording, which only says the others don't let him serve. So the ברייתא is the רבנן: it is only לכתחילה, and בדיעבד his עבודה is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it was already done

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions: (1) the ברייתא is רבי, with no פסול at all. (2) רבי holds a rabbinic פסול, and the ברייתא is the רבנן, who say not לכתחילה but valid בדיעבד.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
רבי holds there is a disqualification by rabbinic law,
and this ברייתא is the view of the רבנן,
and it is only from the start that he may not serve,
but after the fact, his service is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבִּי אִית לֵיהּ פָּסוּל מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version to Step 18 about who authored the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, a כהן under twenty should not serve לכתחילה, but בדיעבד his עבודה is valid.

steps.title: משנה: what is pure in an earthenware vessel is impure in other vessels
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches a reversed pattern between כלי חרס and all other כלים in how they become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that is טהור in a כלי חרס is טמא in all other כלים, and something that is טהור in all other כלים is טמא in a כלי חרס.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a short rule that sounds like a riddle, and the גמרא will explain it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not yet say which situation it means. It only states that the same case gives opposite results for a כלי חרס and for other כלים. The explanation comes in the next step.

phrases.english: MISHNA: That which is pure in an earthenware vessel
is impure in all the other vessels;
that which is pure in all the other vessels
is impure in an earthenware vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, טומאת כלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same case leads to opposite טומאה results for a כלי חרס and for other כלים.

steps.title: ברייתא explains: inside airspace versus outside surface
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה: a כלי חרס becomes טמא through its airspace but not its outside, while other כלים become טמא through their outside but not their airspace.
steps.simpleTranslation: If something טמא is in the airspace of a כלי חרס, the vessel is טמא. If it touches the outside, the vessel stays טהור. Other כלים are the opposite: airspace keeps them טהור, the outside makes them טמא. So the two kinds of vessels give opposite results.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the riddle in the משנה. It shows exactly where the טומאה has to be for each kind of vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס gets טמא only from the inside, even without touching, and never from the outside. Other כלים get טמא only by real contact, so touching the outside counts but hanging in the airspace does not. That is why the משנה's results are reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Airspace, the empty space inside a vessel
Its outer side, the outside surface
It comes out that, so the result is

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a כלי חרס is 'stronger' or 'weaker' overall. It simply becomes טמא in a different way: from its inside, not by contact on the outside.
steps.whatToRemember: כלי חרס: טמא from inside airspace, not from outside. Other כלים: טמא from outside contact, not from airspace alone.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The רבנן taught:
The airspace of an earthenware vessel makes it impure,
phrases.notes: He means: if a source of טומאה lands inside the clay vessel, even without touching its walls.

phrases.english: and its outer side leaves it pure.
The airspace of all other vessels leaves them pure,
and their outer side makes them impure.
It comes out that what is pure in an earthenware vessel
is impure in all other vessels,
and what is pure in all other vessels
is impure in an earthenware vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֲוִיר כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which case the משנה of Step 20 is talking about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס is made טמא through its airspace but not its outside. Other כלים are made טמא through their outside but not their airspace.

steps.title: Asking for the source of these rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where these rules about airspace and outer surface come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה for the rules it just taught. This sets up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated the rules but gave no source. The גמרא now wants to know which פסוק teaches them.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rules in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that a כלי חרס becomes טמא from its airspace, and the opposite rule for other כלים.

steps.title: The word 'תוכו': impure even without touching
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'תוכו' that a כלי חרס becomes טמא when something falls inside it, even without touching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: the פסוק says 'into its inside' (תוכו), meaning the vessel becomes טמא even if the טמא item did not touch it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with a ברייתא about the פסוק on כלי חרס. The key word is 'תוכו', 'its inside'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says טומאה falls 'into its inside,' not 'touches it.' So being inside the airspace is enough to make a כלי חרס טמא, even with no contact. This is the source for the first half of the ברייתא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Its inside, the word in the פסוק about a כלי חרס
Even though it did not touch

phrases.english: As the רבנן taught:
"Its inside,"
even though it did not touch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'תוכו' in the פסוק teaches that a כלי חרס becomes טמא from טומאה inside its airspace, even without contact.

steps.title: Must the impure item actually touch the clay vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא questions its own reading of תוכו: maybe the כלי חרס becomes טמא only if the טומאה touches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you saying the clay vessel is impure even if the impure thing did not touch it? Or maybe it is impure only if it did touch it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops to question the rule it just learned from תוכו. This sets up the next move, where a proof will settle the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 read 'into its inside' (תוכו) as meaning no touching is needed. But 'falling inside' could still mean falling in and landing on the walls or bottom. So the ברייתא asks whether touching is required after all.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps it is only (a formula that raises the other possibility)

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָגַע,
phrases.english: Do you say it is impure even though it did not touch,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the impure thing that fell into the clay vessel.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָגַע?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is impure only if it touched?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָגַע, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָגַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the derivation from תוכו in step 23 by raising the possibility that contact is still required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a כלי חרס become טמא from an impure item in its airspace without contact, or only with contact?

steps.title: Comparing the two uses of 'its inside'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס compares תוכו for making things טמא with תוכו for becoming טמא. Neither one requires touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס says: The word 'its inside' is used about making things impure, and it is also used about becoming impure. When 'its inside' is used about making things impure, no touching is needed. So too, when it is used about becoming impure, no touching is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס answers the question with a word comparison (גזירה שוה) between two uses of תוכו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses תוכו twice. Once it is about the טומאה falling into the כלי, which makes the כלי טמא. Once it is about food inside the כלי, which the כלי makes טמא. We already know that food in the airspace becomes טמא without touching the כלי. The same word teaches the same rule for the כלי itself: the טומאה does not need to touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: to make something else impure (to pass impurity on)
a comparison based on the same word appearing in two places

steps.confusionAlert: לְטַמֵּא and לִיטַּמֵּא look almost the same. לְטַמֵּא means the כלי passes impurity on to food inside it. לִיטַּמֵּא means the כלי itself becomes impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the rule from step 21 that a כלי חרס becomes טמא through its airspace.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Avtolemos says:
'Its inside' is stated about making impure,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:33: 'whatever is in its inside shall be impure.' This is about food inside the vessel.

phrases.english: and 'its inside' is stated about becoming impure,
phrases.notes: The same פסוק: 'into its inside any of them falls.' This is about the vessel itself.

phrases.english: just as 'its inside' that is stated about making impure
applies even though it did not touch,
so too 'its inside' that is stated about becoming impure
applies even though it did not touch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No contact is needed. The meaning of תוכו for becoming טמא is learned from תוכו for passing on טומאה, where contact is not required.

steps.title: How do we know food inside becomes impure without touching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that the proof relied on: food in the airspace of a טמא כלי חרס becomes טמא without touching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, about food inside the vessel, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that the comparison in step 25 depended on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 treated it as known that food in a טמא כלי חרס becomes טמא even without touching the כלי. The גמרא now wants to know where that rule comes from. Without a source, the comparison has nothing to build on.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know it?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: 'There' is the food inside the clay vessel, which becomes impure without touching the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first half of the גזירה שוה in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that food in the airspace of a טמא כלי חרס becomes טמא without contact?

steps.title: The Torah testified about the clay vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן begins his answer by saying that the תורה testified about a כלי חרס. The full explanation continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: The תורה testified about a clay vessel...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן begins to answer the question of step 26. His answer continues in the next section of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far he only gives the opening: the תורה made a special statement about a כלי חרס. The rest of his words will explain how that statement teaches that food inside becomes טמא without touching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:
The Torah testified about a clay vessel

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: הַתּוֹרָה הֵעִידָה עַל כְּלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a special testimony of the תורה about a כלי חרס. The details continue in the next section.
